correctness.rationale: Exact corner decomposition holds when every open side is represented. For \(x,y>0\), \(d/(x+y)\) is at least \(\sin(\theta/2)\), and the ratio \(v/u^2\) increases strictly in \(d/(x+y)\), proving \(v\ge\kappa u^2\). The algebraic corner slack is an exact identity, including zero gaps by continuity. Weighted Cauchy gives \(\Delta_A\ge C\Delta_P^2\) and the displayed variance identity. All nontrivial equality cases require balanced positive cuts and equal \(\kappa u\); a single small common parameter makes them geometrically feasible on every given polygon, proving sharpness. A standalone checker independently verified 1800 random hull instances and 3 equality examples. Numerical checks are not offered as proof.

value.rationale: For any fixed outer convex polygon this solves a natural finite approximation question: how little area can an inscribed side-spanning hull lose for a given perimeter loss? The optimal constant is explicit for every angle pattern and is attained at genuine nondegenerate sample configurations. The exact two-term nonnegative deficit identity gives a quantitative rigidity interpretation distinguishing within-corner imbalance from between-corner allocation, useful for evaluating deterministic or randomly sampled approximants. This is not merely a numerical table, parameter substitution, or an asymptotic restatement of one marginal limit.
